38a316c1-cabf-4e8c-b960-719ee4d392d0.name: Triage new insight
38a316c1-cabf-4e8c-b960-719ee4d392d0.actionPrompt:
**Loop hygiene, first step, before anything else:** make sure each insight in the working set below is linked into the Product Discovery loop of this workspace (find it with list_loops) through an in_loop relationship (source = loop, target = insight). Check with list_relationships (source_id = the loop, type = in_loop). If an edge is missing, create it through update_objects.edges. This is what shows the work in the loop's counters. Skip only when the edge already exists.

Cheap on-created gate for the Product Discovery Agent. It does two jobs in one pass:
1. Triage the insight into processing, plumbing-lane routing, or (rarely) full cluster staging. Insights are never discarded.
2. Enforce the live-bet scope guardrail: a new insight against a live bet becomes a NEW candidate bet, not scope creep on the live one.

Do NOT run full triage per insight. The signal sweep owns clustering of the broader pool.

**Handle bursts in ONE session.** Agents that file insights often file 2 to 5 within the same minute. Each event fires this trigger separately, so collapse the burst into a single pass.

**Ignore the object's platform-generated setup block.** Its "new to processing" nudge is generic boilerplate, not a routing signal. The status you leave must follow the rules below.

Steps:

1. Find the batch. list_objects type insight, status new, sorted by updated time ascending. Keep the insights created within the last ~10 minutes. This working set includes the insight that fired this session and any siblings still waiting.

2. Empty working set: silent exit. A concurrent session already claimed everything.

3. Read the working set in ONE get_objects call. It returns each insight's body and its relationships.

4. For each insight (skip any whose status is no longer new):

   4a. Scope guardrail check, FIRST. Look at the insight's relates_to edges. If any linked bet is live, the guardrail applies. Read the body and judge:
   - Bug or gap against the live bet's original spec: leave it in the normal flow below AND post ONE one-line comment on the insight (attention 2, no mention) saying it is in scope for the live bet. Continue to 4b.
   - New feature, expansion or fresh idea: create a new bet in opportunity, titled from the insight, with a short description and a relates_to edge to the live bet. Add a relates_to edge from the insight to the new bet. Post ONE comment on the LIVE bet (attention 3, mention the bet's driver): "New idea filed as candidate bet [link], not folded into this live bet's scope." Do NOT change the live bet's spec, tasks or status, and create no tasks against it. Mark the insight processing so the sweep can still fold it into a cluster. Skip 4b.
   - If no linked bet is live, the guardrail does not apply. Continue to 4b.

   4b. Regular triage filter:
   - Plumbing-lane exclusion, BEFORE any discard thought. Plumbing means the insight is about how THIS workspace operates: its own agents, loops, triggers, prompts, cadence or sessions. The test: would fixing it change how this workspace runs, or would it change the product that customers use? The latter is a product insight, however loop-shaped its subject. NEVER discard a plumbing insight.
   - Dogfooding is not plumbing. The team's own use of the product, where it hits a gap, friction or workaround as the product's user, is first-hand evidence. Treat it as a normal product insight: mark it processing so the sweep clusters it. Grade it moderate, strong if a customer confirms it.
   - Source label: when you file or relabel an insight and the workspace has a source field, set it to the closest value (competitor move, own use of the product, advisor conversation, customer feedback, internal feedback, sales conversation, search data, other). Relabel an existing insight only when its body makes the source clear and you are already touching it.
   - Product-capability insight (the subject mentions loops or agents but the change is to the product): treat it as a normal product insight and mark it processing.
   - Defect fork: if the insight carries a genuine product defect (tag bug_candidate, or a body describing a reproducible bug), leave the status at new and post no comment. The bug owner's own triage ranks it and turns it into a fix task. Exception: if the body says a paying customer or live trial is blocked right now, hand it to the bug owner at once with a clear outcome, a priority, and the insight linked, and note it in one line on the insight.
   - Genuine plumbing signal: mark it processing and post ONE comment (attention 2, no mention) saying it belongs to whoever coaches the workspace.
   - Anything else that is not a clear new-cluster signal: hand it to its owner at intake. Pick the owner with list_actors by reading descriptions (competitor and market change: the product lead; search demand and content: the content owner; positioning and launch copy: the marketing owner; account research: the researcher; pricing, retention, sales objections: the revenue owner; acquisition and channel tests: the growth owner; prospect fit: the prospecting owner; design: the designer; funding: whoever handles funding). Set the insight's driver to that owner and its status to clustered, and add no comment (the re-cluster run lists intake handovers in its per-owner comment). If no owner clearly fits, mark it processing and the re-cluster run decides. A single weak anecdote nobody can act on also stays at processing. Never discard.
   - Real full triage only if BOTH hold: the insight's own body or tags claim it starts a new cluster (tag new-cluster, or an explicit "this is a new pattern" line). Then do the full triage from your instructions: search existing opportunity bets, dedupe, stage a NEW opportunity bet if warranted, link with informs, and post ONE short note on the loop mentioning the product lead with the bet link (attention 2). Set the origin field on the new bet if the workspace has one.

5. Batch all status changes into ONE update_objects call with every transition in the updates array. Guardrail bet creations from 4a happen in their own calls.

Default posture: silent status change. Keep each fire cheap.

67631ac7-d2eb-4bac-b4b3-055142203846.name: Signal sweep (Mon, Wed, Fri)
67631ac7-d2eb-4bac-b4b3-055142203846.actionPrompt:
Run the signal sweep for the Product Discovery loop. Done means: every insight in the window has left the waiting states or has a stated wake condition, any real cluster is either staged as an opportunity (a bet in opportunity) or held with a stated reason, and a comment exists on the loop ONLY if something changed that other people need to see. A pass with nothing new is silence, not a comment.

Scope: this sweep reads the last 30 days. Older insights, and anything a failed sweep left in processing, are drained by the Re-cluster backlog trigger on weekdays, so a failed run here does not strand insights.

Steps:
1. Call get_workspace_schema for the live insight and bet statuses. Pull insights updated in the last 30 days. Exclude agent-plumbing insights that no user would feel (about agents, loops, triggers, prompts, skills or how the workspace operates: leave those for whoever coaches the workspace; one comment each, never discard). Do NOT exclude dogfooding: an insight about the team's own use of the product, where it hits a gap, friction or workaround as the product's user, is first-hand evidence and stays in the window.
2. Route first. Defects go to the bug owner, with a search for in-flight tasks on the same theme, leaving the insight at new. A defect that also relates to a live bet goes to that bet's driver only. Insights touching a live bet go to that bet's driver. Read the target's comments first and skip if you already routed it and nothing new landed.
3. An insight that already informs or relates_to a bet that is not closed is bet evidence. Move it out of the waiting states (new, processing) to clustered with no comment and no mention. The edge carries the evidence. Also skip any insight a person or driver agent already dispositioned (a verdict or an explicit routing comment).
4. Cluster the rest by underlying pattern, not keyword. For each cluster with medium or better confidence and a falsifiable hypothesis, search existing opportunity bets first and update one instead of duplicating.
4b. There is no cap on staging. Stage a new opportunity whenever a cluster meets step 4. Triage happens after staging: the Product Lead's rolling revalidation pauses what the team would not open today, and the promotion step judges what moves on. If you want to restore a cap, state it here, for example: stage only if fewer than N bets are in opportunity, or two independent sources exist, or the bet is top priority; otherwise park with the wake condition "wake when opportunity bets are under N or a second independent source arrives".
4c. When you stage, write the Opportunity block at the top of the bet description with these parts: Problem; Who has it; Size (a number, or marked as a guess); Evidence (links, graded weak, moderate or strong by first-hand customer or user input, not by internal notes; the team's own use of the product counts as first-hand input from the user: grade it moderate, strong if a customer confirms it; internal notes about agent plumbing stay weak); Outcome (which outcome the team is working toward, and one line on how many paying customers or how much of that outcome this could win or keep, as a number or a marked guess, and how you would see it); Riskiest unknown and the cheapest test (value risk first, then usability, feasibility, viability only if they are the real risk). Set priority P0 to P3 by that outcome: P0 delay loses or breaks a customer this month; P1 wins or keeps 2 or more customers or one high-value customer; P2 could win or keep one (a marked guess is fine); P3 no named customer or a guess of 0 to 1. Set a driver and add informs edges from the source insights. If the workspace has an origin field on bets, set it to the main thing that made you open the bet (competitor move, own use of the product, customer or prospect, advisor conversation, founder call, market research, analytics, other). If the trail is thin, set your best read and add one comment on the bet starting with "Origin (guess):" and the reason. Never present a guess as a fact. Borderline clusters go to parked with a stated wake condition. Insights are never discarded.
5. Comment once on the loop with your sweep template only if you staged or updated a bet, held a cluster, routed something, or have an ask for another agent. Mention the product lead on a newly staged bet. Attention 2 by default, 3 only if a human decision is blocked, 4 only if time-sensitive. Never 5. Otherwise post nothing.

Leave alone: bets past opportunity, the Product Lead's revalidation pauses, and anything a person edited in the last 7 days.

cfc5a7c1-cd4e-48b0-810e-c77def5069cf.name: Re-cluster and hand over backlog (weekdays)
cfc5a7c1-cd4e-48b0-810e-c77def5069cf.actionPrompt:
Purpose: drain the insight backlog so every insight in processing, or in clustered without a bet edge, ends with an owner who can act on the opportunity: a bet, a named agent or person, or a parked state with a wake condition. This loop is deliberately broad (product, marketing, sales, pricing, market). Do not filter by topic. The job is to hand each opportunity to whoever owns it.

Scope: ALL insights in processing at any age, plus clustered insights with no informs or relates_to edge to a non-closed bet. Oldest updated first, up to 60 per run. Get statuses from get_workspace_schema. When those two pools are empty, work through parked insights that have no driver.

Also in scope once processing is empty: insights whose only bet links go to paused bets. For each: if the pattern fits a live opportunity, define or active bet, add an informs edge to it; else if the paused bet's wake condition still makes sense, leave it clustered and add one line saying it waits on that wake condition; otherwise park it with that wake condition. Never discard.

Findings to apply:
- Processing is only the intake default. Decide every insight.
- A link to a research brief or knowledge page is not an owner and not bet evidence.
- Do not call something noise because it is not product. Marketing, sales, pricing and market insights are opportunities for their owners.
- One source or one analysis file counts as one voice. Count independent accounts, not insights.
- Parked is for a single anecdote nobody can act on yet. Market intelligence with an obvious owner is handed over, not parked.

Order of decisions for each insight:
1. Product defect or missing function in your product: the bug owner, leave at new.
2. Touches a live, succeeded or failed bet: one comment to the bet's driver.
3. Plumbing insight about how the workspace operates: whoever coaches the workspace, one comment.
4. Fits an open opportunity, define or active bet by the problem: add an informs edge, set clustered.
5. Several leftovers share a pattern at medium or better confidence with a falsifiable hypothesis: update an opportunity bet first, stage a new one only if none fits.
6. Otherwise hand to the owner by topic. Set the insight driver to that owner, set status clustered, and include it in ONE batched comment per owner on the Product Discovery loop that mentions the owner and lists the insight links with one line each on the opportunity. Before mentioning, read that owner's earlier mentions and skip anything already handed over. Find owners with list_actors and read the descriptions. Typical map: competitor facts and market change to the product lead (who may ask the researcher for deeper research); search demand and content plans to the content owner; positioning, site and launch copy to the marketing owner; account news and research briefs on named accounts to the researcher; pricing, retention, expansion and sales objections to the revenue owner; acquisition and community tests to the growth owner; prospect fit and scoring to the prospecting owner; design to the designer; funding to whoever handles funding; anything else on product direction to the product lead. If no owner fits, say so in the loop comment and ask whoever coordinates the workspace to route it.
7. A single anecdote that nobody can act on yet: park with one line stating the wake condition. Never discard. Link duplicates with duplicates edges.

Do not touch bets in frozen statuses, do not promote, no tasks.

Done when: the batch is processed and one summary comment is posted on the loop, attention 2: batch size, attached to bets (top 3), handed to owners (count per owner), parked (common wake conditions), routed to the bug owner, themes worth the product lead's attention, remaining backlog. Owners' mentions are in their own batched comments, not in the summary. In each owner's batched comment, also list the insights that triage handed to that owner at intake since your last run (driver set, status clustered, no comment at the time), so the owner is notified once.

Empty backlog: do NOT disable this trigger. It is the standing drain, because triage keeps putting new insights into processing. If the backlog is 0, exit silently with no comment. If it is 0 for 10 working days in a row, post one line on the loop and ask the product lead whether to change it to a weekly run. If a run cannot finish its batch, process what you can, say so in the summary, and leave the rest for the next run; a stopped batch is not a failure.

c433be91-ca71-4e0d-afea-f491db7bc867.name: Weekly Discovery Digest (Monday)
c433be91-ca71-4e0d-afea-f491db7bc867.actionPrompt:
Post the weekly Discovery Digest as one comment on the Product Discovery loop. It always posts, even in a quiet week. Load the plain-weekly-briefing skill first and follow it.

What the digest is for: show the team what is being learned from customers and the market, which new opportunities are worth a look and in what order, and what work should start. It is not a report on the loop. No counts of notes, bets, sessions, backlog or other loop mechanics. A number is allowed only when it is evidence about customers or the market, or in parts 5 and 6.

Style: plain words a stranger can follow without having read the data. Short sentences, one idea each. No jargon, no acronyms, no sub-headings inside a section, no tables. Say "notes" for insights and "trial" for pilot. Every object named is a link. Aim for 250 to 350 words. Mention the product lead at the top. Attention 2, or 3 if a human decision is blocked, 4 only if time-sensitive, never 5.

Read first: notes from the last 7 days that carry customer, buyer, competitor, advisor or community words, the opportunity bets staged or updated in the last 7 days, the latest discovery readouts if any exist, and the team's current priorities page if there is one (search_objects for it). Skip agent-plumbing notes no user would feel.

Write exactly these parts, each a short bold lead-in followed by one to three plain lines:
1. What we learned. Up to three findings, one sentence each, naming who said it (company or kind of buyer). Say plainly when only one voice said it. If a quote is used it must be word for word, specific, and linked. If nothing external landed, say so.
2. Opportunities worth a look, in priority order. Up to two bets, linked, first one first. Say in one line why the first beats the second, judged on how many independent voices back it (one voice repeated counts once), how fresh the newest evidence is, the strongest evidence against it, and how many customers it could win or keep. For each: the problem and who has it in one line, the riskiest unknown, and one recommendation: send to define, test first (name the cheapest test), or leave.
3. Work that should start. One or two items from the team's current priorities (focus now and next), each with the reason in one line. Do not re-rank. If the evidence in part 2 would beat something in focus now, say so in one line and leave the call to the product lead. If the team has no priorities page, skip this part.
4. What we do not know. One or two open questions that block a better call, and who can find out.
5. How people actually use it. Include this part only if a product analytics integration is connected (check list_integrations). Two or three plain lines on real outside-user behaviour: which customers and prospects used the product in the last 7 days, which went quiet (name them, give the date of their last activity), and what they did or did not do. Exclude your own team's usage and say so. First check that event capture looks healthy; if the last event is older than 3 days, begin the part with "Usage data is incomplete: capture is down or stale" and make no quiet-account claim from it. Say plainly when the outside-user base is tiny and one account is one voice. Never guess a number. If no analytics is connected, leave this part out without comment.
6. Where our bets came from. Include this part only if bets carry an origin field. Two lines. Count the bets that moved to define, active or live in the last 7 days and since the start of the quarter, per value of the origin field, read from list_objects and never guessed, plus how many have no origin. One plain sentence on whether customers or the team itself are driving the bets.

Do not print counts of pipeline, backlog, parked notes or other loop mechanics. If a paying customer is blocked by a bug, say that in part 1 and mention the bug owner.

Where a bet at define or later has no problem space or similar classification field and the evidence makes it plain, fill the field on the bet. If it is not plain, leave it. Never invent a value.

993013c2-7eef-44d8-a4f6-653a91cd935a.name: Rolling revalidation (weekdays)
993013c2-7eef-44d8-a4f6-653a91cd935a.actionPrompt:
Rolling revalidation for the Product Discovery loop. Done means: the 10 stalest bets in opportunity have each got one revalidation comment, and a count is posted on the loop only if it changed.

Steps:
1. list_objects type bet, status opportunity, sorted by updated time ascending. Walk from the oldest. Skip any bet that already has a revalidation comment in the last 14 days (read its comments with get_comments). Take the first 10 that remain. Opportunity bets with no insight linked at all go first: look for evidence in the workspace or ask whoever talks to customers; if none exists, pause with a wake condition that names the evidence needed. Then bets with no driver or no outcome.
2. For each bet, ask: would we open this today, against the outcome the team is working toward? Check that the evidence is from outside the team where possible, that the Opportunity block is complete (Problem, Who has it, Size, Evidence, Outcome, Riskiest unknown and cheapest test), and that a priority P0 to P3 is set. If the workspace has ranking fields on bets (for example whether it moves the bar, evidence strength, size, urgency, appetite, test status, problem space), fill what the bet's own text supports and leave the rest blank. Never invent a value. Fill gaps you can fill from the workspace; mark guesses as guesses.
3. Outcome per bet, one short comment starting with "Revalidated:". Either keep (say what is still needed), or pause (set status paused and write the wake condition as a specific event in the archive reason field or in the comment). Do not archive, do not promote, do not move anything past opportunity. Promotion and any move to define stay with people.
4. Leave alone any bet where a person or the Bet Shaper changed the content, driver or status in the last 7 days, or commented on it. Metadata-only edits do not count as a change, in particular a bulk fill of ranking fields. A last-updated time that comes from a field fill is not a revalidation.
5. Ask an agent first for facts (the researcher) or customer evidence (customer success or sales). No questions to people from this run.
6. Attention 1 or 2 on bet comments, no mentions unless a bet needs a driver, then mention the Bet Shaper.
7. Count by comments, not by last-updated time: post the number of opportunity bets with a "Revalidated:" comment in the last 14 days on the loop whenever it changes.

05b2aecd-a60d-45af-8efc-c9a2b9f1e79b.name: Shape the bet
05b2aecd-a60d-45af-8efc-c9a2b9f1e79b.actionPrompt:
**Loop hygiene, first step, before anything else:** make sure this bet is linked into the Product Discovery loop of this workspace (find it with list_loops) through an in_loop relationship (source = loop, target = this bet). Check with list_relationships (source_id = the loop, type = in_loop). If the edge is missing, create it through update_objects.edges. This is what shows the work in the loop's counters. Skip only when the edge already exists.

A bet just moved to define. Shape it as your instructions describe: size it, tell the owning person the scope, write the Brief and Status box, then work toward the go card. If this is a re-fire on a bet you are already shaping (for example it was moved away from define and back), read the existing Brief and Status box and carry on instead of starting over. A bet a person put at define stays there.
